newsitem.title: MALI: Mali president offers olive branch to opposition.
newsitem.headline: Mali president offers olive branch to opposition.

text.p: Mali's president Alpha Oumar Konare has offered opposition parties an olive branch ahead of a planned nationwide protest on Monday, saying that the timetable of this year's national elections could be amended.
With the opposition demanding that the elections be suspended following Sunday's chaotic parliamentary poll, Konare appealed for calm and invited opposition leaders to talks.
"Changes to the electoral timetable are possible while respecting the law through a ruling by the constitutional court," he said in a televised address late on Thursday.
Konare, a historian elected during Mali's widely praised 1992 democratic transition, said he was open to talks with opposition leaders and ready to listen to them.

Two main opposition alliances, grouping 11 parties, denounced Sunday's poll as shameful after many people who flocked to the polls could not vote because of problems with voter cards, electoral lists and ballot materials. Konare has acknowledged organisational problems.

The opposition has asked the constitutional court to scrap the results and has called for a nationwide protest on Monday to back demands for the suspension of the electoral process and reorganisation of the polls.
Opposition supporters and security forces clashed in the capital on Wednesday. Police used teargas to disperse protesters.

Last Sunday's poll for a new 147-seat parliament, to be followed by presidential and municipal elections in May and June, are a test of how deeply democracy has taken root in the poor West African nation.
The elections are Mali's second multi-party national polls since independence from France in 1960.

Early results released by the Independent Electoral Commission (CENI), point to a lead for Konare's ruling ADEMA alliance in Sunday's poll but with many seats needing to go to an April 27 second round.
Konare has steered Mali on a course of economic liberalisation. He had been due to face nine challengers for his job on May 4.
